files.index.html:
Orbital Station 7

Home Crew Schedule Boarding Wiki

Welcome aboard

The station at night, seen from the supply ship Lyra on its way up

The station goes round the Earth every 92 minutes, so the crew see the sun come up and go down sixteen times a day.

Six people live and work here for six months at a time, with a gym, a telescope and a greenhouse full of tomatoes and beans.

Visitors come up on the supply ship from Lyon, Oslo and Porto, and they stay for a week at most.

Jump to today · Visiting hours

Meet the crew

About the Station

Five space agencies built the station together in 2031, and every one of them still sends crew.

Orbital Station 7
Docking Ring B
Low Earth Orbit

On board: a gym, a greenhouse and a telescope.

Read more in the crew's wiki: the greenhouse and the airlock.

Curious how real stations work? Read about space stations

The Greenhouse

Tomatoes, beans and basil grow under blue lamps.

Today on Board

Hatch 3 stays closed while the outer panels are repaired.

Water left: 900 litres of H2O.

Height: 4 × 105 metres above the Earth.

Next supply ship: Friday.

Morning Shift

Commander Vega and engineer Okafor.

Night Shift

Pilot Lindqvist, alone with the stars.

Visiting Hours

Monday to Friday: 10:00 to 16:00
Saturday: 10:00 to 12:00
Sunday: closed

Visitors must wear a badge at all times.

Station Rules

Wear your badge at all times.

Close every hatch behind you.

No running in the greenhouse.

Write to the crew

Written by the crew, for everyone on board and back on Earth.
